<color=#ffd780>August 17, 2024</color>
Hello, Traveler!
Today, we'll be introducing the "Children of Echoes," one of Natlan's six tribes. Word has it that the mines near the tribes hide a lot of treasure!
Children of Echoes

The
are a tribe living alongside the Tepetlisaurs and located in the Tequemecan Valley. They were founded about two thousand years ago by the Natlan hero, Ixquieh, who overthrew the ancient dragons along with Natlan's first Pyro Archon. The Tequemecan Valley is rich in solid phlogiston and various fossils, making the Nanatzcayan famous for their mines, weapons manufacturing, and jewelry making. The Children of Echoes work closely with stone, which is one of the tribe's symbols. The Tepetlisaurs, thanks to their digging abilities, help locate the best ore and gemstones. The tribe is also known for its dances and holds a daily "Drillbit Dance" competition. The current chief of the Nanatzcayan is Pacal, who prefers not to interfere in the lives of the tribe members but rather to support and protect them.

In addition to weapons and jewelry, some of the tribe's blacksmiths can forge Ancient Names. Natlan is a nation of heroes whose valiant deeds are preserved and passed down through the generations as stories. The Wayob of each tribe selects powerful warriors and awards them with
carved into obsidian. All obsidian in Natlan comes from the Children of Echoes, and only a few merchants sell it outside of the tribe. An Ancient Name can be seen as a "title" and a sign of the stories of all who bear it. By mentioning an Ancient Name, Natlanese are reminded of the epic sagas of the heroes of the past. In addition, the Tocaitl allows the stories of the past to be carefully preserved, like relics passed down through the generations. The Wayob decide who is worthy of inheriting an Ancient Name. Once a successor is selected, the Name becomes theirs to bear, and their deeds are then preserved within it. As time passes, Ancient Names come to represent the heroic deeds of more and more bearers, and their value becomes even more profound. In turn, the accomplishments preserved within it serve as an inspiration for the next generation of successors. The Ancient Names are endowed with the ability to read information from the Ley Lines, while the Wayob act as a transmitter and help the bearer perceive this information.

Engravers of the Ancient Names can only forge them with the Wayob's consent, as all the memories it carries are stored in the Ley Lines, and a Wayob's help is needed to extract them. In order to convey the meaning of an Ancient Name as accurately as possible, engravers must verify the deeds of people who are long dead. This usually comes down to checking scrolls, but even then, it is difficult to tell how accurate the records are. Incorporating a fictitious story or lie into an Ancient Name will render it flawed, potentially causing cognitive problems for the bearer. Forging an Ancient Name is an act of creation and can cost the life of the engraver. The engraver must take disparate concepts from across the Night Kingdom and condense them into a heroic epic. If the Ancient Name is like a seed, then the life of the craftsman is the outer shell, serving as its protection. Once that process is complete, the seed will sprout, and having served its purpose, the outer shell will gradually disappear.

Forging an Ancient Name for a Natlanese is no easy task, but creating an Ancient Name for an outlander is an even greater challenge. In all of Natlan's history, only one new name has ever been forged for an outsider, the Traveler. They played a crucial role in the battle against the Abyss, so the Pyro Archon decided to create an Ancient Name for them to ensure their safety. The name engraver, Xilonen, agreed to take on this task, knowing that it could cost her life. With a gift from the Lord of the Night herself, Xilonen was able to record the stories of all the Traveler's acquaintances in Natlan about their exploits and create a new Ancient Name,
while preserving her life.

Although the forging of an Ancient Name requires the consent of the Wayob, there are ways to create it without their participation. An engraver from the Children of Echoes, Tlazolli, used the Blazegem Inscription to create a vast repository of memories for her deceased daughter. The new Ancient Name was meant to unite all the extracted memories of the people associated with her, but Tlazolli did not take into account that people's memories can store feelings and emotions. Thus, the image of her daughter was distorted and tainted by the Abyss.

customize.text: Ixquieh

Well over two thousand years ago, ancient dragons ruled Natlan, and people lived under their oppression. At that time, a woman named Ixquieh lived in the Tequemecan Valley. She had been separated from her twin brother, Ahpub, since childhood. Their father died at the hands of the Dragonlord, and their mother sacrificed herself to protect her children. If not for the assistance of the Collective of Plenty and the clans of the mines, Ahpub and Ixquieh's reunion would have been impossible. In the years when the war chiefs of the tribes had abandoned their noble cause of slaying wicked dragons and were plunged into endless warfare, a hero named Xbalanque, unprophesied, unchronicled by any plan, appeared. He rose from the black lands and walked from tribe to tribe, wearing a crown woven from golden flowers and wielding a great blade of obsidian. Thus, the Grand Alliance was founded, uniting all the tribes. Among those who joined Xbalanque were Ixquieh and Ahpub. Together with other heroes, they went to war against the ancient dragons, and when Xbalanque slew the
they swore an oath at his body. They swore to end the death, destruction, and suffering so that the powerful could no longer oppress the weak, and light would shine upon the valley. Ixquieh founded the Children of Echoes and received the Ancient Name

<color=#ffffffd9>"O Brave Hero, should thy path lead to executing fell dragons"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"O Brave Hero, if your path leads to stamping out suffering"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"We swear upon sacred Yaxche and the ancestors"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Ahpub's blowdarts and Ixquieh's forge-fires shall be yours to use."</color>

One day, Ixquieh and her brother challenged a dragon who had proclaimed itself the sun god. They forged an imitation gemstone that seemed perfectly identical to the original, with a fire previously unknown to mortals. They fooled the earthquake-causing great dragon into drinking the elixir, which stripped it of its power, and the dragon was buried alive amidst the mountains. After overthrowing the Flamelord, Ixquieh studied the dragons' machinery to use it for the benefit of humanity. The dragons used phlogiston-forging techniques to forge various materials directly from phlogiston, and Ixquieh, dubbed the "Hero of the Forged Flame," rediscovered this method. Later, she set her workshop on fire to prevent Och-Kan from gaining possession of her research, and the Hero of the Forged Flame's entire legacy was destroyed.

When Xbalanque entered the Sacred Flame, he left the rule of Natlan to his best friend, Och-Kan. The latter despised everything associated with dragons and persecuted anyone who showed even the slightest sympathy for their civilization. The surviving dragons and their descendants were forced into hiding. Among them was the Eleventh Dragonlord, "Mirror of the Dawning Morn," the proudest of all the sovereign rulers and the most hostile toward humanity. When the Pyro Sovereign fell, she could not accept the dragons' defeat and plunged into utter despair and madness. Deprived of her territory, she was tormented by the question of whether to strike back at humanity and exact revenge or search for a new home. In the end, her mind split into two parts: one, the sovereign ruler who swore revenge against humanity; the other, a malfunction, who longed to seek a new home. The sovereign ruler approached Ixquieh and Lianca, the founder of the Flower-Feather Clan, to trick them into destroying the "malfunction," but they saw through her. Lianca turned the Eleventh Lord's plan against her, sealing her within a dragon prison. Ixquieh implanted the Moon Wheel, left to Lianca by her adoptive mother, into the core of the "malfunction." They sent the latter on its journey, hoping that even after a thousand years, it would find a home.

After the beginning of Och-Kan's reign, Ixquieh and Ahpub grew distant. When the ruler of the Grand Alliance ordered the extermination of the Saurians, only Ahpub answered the call. He went to the Children of Echoes to demand the surrender of the Saurians, but Ixquieh refused. After several days of confrontation, the hero invited his sister to talk at the place of their reunion, intending to remind her of the oath. When Ixquieh told her brother about the betrayal of Xbalanque's ideals, he put a blade to her neck. Ixquieh threw herself directly onto her brother's sword, attempting to force him into taking their lives together. Ahpub, holding his sister in his arms, entered the incinerating fire and perished with her. On that day, both Teteocan and Nanatzcayan lost their leaders.

customize.text: The Fall of Ochkanatlan

When the followers of the first Pyro Archon built the Grand Alliance on the ruins of the dragon civilization, Och-Kan discovered that beneath the flooded ruins lay a core capable of powering the entire city. He asked to send one person from ten families of each tribe to build irrigation structures to drain the water, and the Children of Echoes' master, Manqu, answered the call. Deep within the ruins, the workers unearthed a statue from the dragon era, which sealed one of the sovereign rulers. Furthermore, the workers began dying from the contamination, forcing the ruins to be sealed with a stone slab and the entire excavation site to be burned. Manqu was among those trapped near the dragon statue. As he was lying under the grotesque statue, doomed to die, surrounded by all-consuming flames in Och-Kan's fire, he suddenly saw a young woman whose face was more beautiful than the purest crystal and whose eyes were more beautiful than the purest turquoise. Despite her beauty, her face was so nauseatingly repulsive. Her smile was laced with a cruel and arrogant malice. The craftsman opened his mouth to beg her to save him, but his lips burned beyond all recognition, and he could not utter a single word. The woman held his face in her hand, and from those turquoise eyes, golden tears fell into Manqu's eyes. He then saw a colossal creation, far larger than the rolling mountains, floating in the sky like a volcanic cloud; countless metal birds greedily sucking dark blood and shadows driven by flowing flames, climbing high from distant horizons to the moon up in the sky. She sneered by his ear that people could crawl around beneath the heavens, trembling away while seeking their inglorious graves, and that the ancient dragons had fought an inveterate foe as formidable as an entire world. Through the turquoise eyes of the woman, the craftsman saw naught but endless, unfathomable darkness and void that no language could describe. Then, Manqu screamed at the top of his lungs and, stumbling, crawled towards the secret path, but his scream was drowned in the laughter of the woman. When the craftsman woke up, he was completely alone. He didn't know if the woman existed or if it was delirium, or if it was tears or drops of water that fell from the giant dragon statue behind her, but he was alive.
While Manqu was passing the time in dirty taverns, he met the daughter of the mines, Sakkuk, who was looking for the craftsman who had created a masterful turquoise feather for her father. She bore the Ancient Name of her predecessor, Ixquieh, and was among those who followed the scarlet-eyed youth from the Flower-Feather Clan to overthrow the tyrant of Cinder City. The scars of a burn by a raging blaze marred the half of the master's face that was hidden under a hat, the flesh a melted slurry of blood, but Sakkuk was not afraid and handed him the plume. When he learned that the man to whom he gave the feather was the girl's father, the craftsman agreed to serve her and her master. When their rebellion succeeded, the people spoke of the mastermind behind the plan, a skilled artisan who remained nameless. Manqu planned to disconnect the city from the power source and turn off the core to lead the youth with scarlet eyes to Och-Kan's throne room.

The scarlet-eyed youth, guided through numerous trials, was able to defeat the tyrant of the forbidden city. Still, the artisan, Manqu, could not escape the burning city because the Flower-Feather Clan had walled up the secret exits. To emulate Xbalanque, the first human to ascend, he sacrificed his heart and then returned from the Night Kingdom, becoming the second Pyro Archon of Natlan. So that people would know that every human can become the god that guides them, the scarlet-eyed youth asked Sakkuk, who was in love with him, to erase his name from history.
After Sakkuk returned to her tribe, she asked to make the long-dulled feather for her again. She promised the craftsman that when the time came, she would give them a turquoise crown in return. It was after witnessing the crooked corpse agonizingly hunched beneath the black beast's butcher blade that she understood that the crown would wait alone for its master. For many years, she collected jewelry that was signed by Manqu, gifting those who presented them with precious gems. Even if it were a forgery, she would take it all the same. The mistress of the mines did not want the crude forgeries to stain the good name of an artisan who created the originals, and deceivers with forgeries were always punished. At the end of her life, Sakkuk collected all the works bearing Manqu's name and walked into the dark night, never to return. According to legend, on the next day, the people stood under the tree where she had placed the turquoise crown and swore an oath to follow her final orders, blotting from history the name of the masterful craftsman she took away with her.

customize.text: The Cataclysm

Five hundred years ago, the Cataclysm occurred in Teyvat. A black tide of the Abyss engulfed all seven nations, and Natlan was no exception. At that time, the chief of the Children of Echoes was Maghan Sundjatta, heir to the Ancient Name of Ixquieh and Sakkuk. Despite the looming danger, the tribal leaders were mired in conflict and unable to unite. When the exiled Tenoch decided to mediate, Sundjatta, along with his Saurian companion, Muhuru, joined him, along with five other heroes bearing the Ancient Names of the first Pyro Archon's companions. Although the leader of the mines once appealed to the Pyro Archon to support Tenoch's exile for the sake of all the tribes and to avoid further conflict, he knew that this battle could be Natlan's last.
<color=#ffffffd9>"If you are so determined to go, then I have no reason not to accompany you, but do not involve my tribe."</color>

Sundjatta never returned from the war, dying alongside other heroes of Natlan. When the chief departed for the future Mare Jivari, the Abyss spilled over near the Sulfurous Veins belonging to the Children of Echoes. Elder Traore was the only one left to protect the tribe, so he set out with his warriors and their Saurian companions. They were joined by two warriors from the
without gods, Zephaniah and Irizar. Together, they managed to contain the Abyss with phlogiston spikes called the Shadow Pins. The warriors from Khaenri'ah, at the cost of their lives, remained to contain the Abyss on the Land of Miraid Megaliths, sealed with Iridescent Inscriptions. They wanted to serve as a warning to others to never let their guard down, so they asked Traore to be remembered in history as cowards, enemies, and rogues. For five hundred years, the names of these warriors have been associated with evil and used to frighten children: <color=#ffffffd9>"If you don't stop crying, the ghosts of the Khaenri'ahn soldiers will follow the sound and track down your shadow..."</color> But in reality, Zephaniah and Irizar were heroes who sacrificed themselves so that others could live.

Ten years after the Cataclysm, when the Abyss was defeated, a legend arose in Natlan about the Jade of Return, an ancient treasure kept in the forbidden city of Ochkanatlan, capable of destroying the Abyss forever. Several tribe members, including Titu, joined an adventure team and traveled to Ochkanatlan. When they approached the flying ship, Tonatiuh, it turned out the Jade of Return was a myth created by the
In reality, the Jade of Return was half a core needed to activate an ancient dragon weapon capable of destroying the Abyss at the cost of all life in Natlan. The Jade of Return was sealed so that only humans could remove it, so Waxaklahun Ubah Kan himself could not obtain it. Thus, he created a legend to attract humans. At the legendary Tonatiuh and in the forbidden city, the entire group perished in the battle with Och-Kan, who was corrupted by the Abyss. The Sage of the Stolen Flame later even used Titu's image as a disguise. When the dragon's life force was exhausted five hundred years later, Titu awoke from his long slumber and was granted the right to a second life.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Strange... I am not someone who should have appeared in the 'present'... Sorry, I know you might not understand, but I... have had many pasts, so many memories of lives led... But none of them 'me.'</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>The life of the one named 'Titu' was akin to a dream in which he could not control his own body, a dream from which he has only just awakened... Only now does he hear the Lord of the Night's call...</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Was this... your doing? That sense of being controlled has faded. Hmm... Yes. Perhaps this shall be the final life of the one named 'Titu.'</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Thank you, outlander hero... Haha. Let's live this life out in peace, shall we? Being a storyteller sounds pretty sweet in that regard…"</color>

customize.text: The War with the Abyss

Although the Abyss was defeated during the Cataclysm, it did not vanish completely but rather retreated into the depths of the Night Kingdom. Gradually, over the course of five hundred years, the Abyss began to attack Natlan. The Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame and the Night Warden Wars were initiated to bolster the protection of the Sacred Flame. During the Pilgrimage, participants first competed against each other under the guidance of bearers of an Ancient Name, and then members of the winning teams earned the right to fight one-on-one duels. The Pilgrimage selected the strongest warriors from all the tribes to fight the Abyss in defense of their homeland. Their names and deeds were captured in epic tales, and thanks to the Archon's blessing, called the Ode of Resurrection, the victors could be resurrected even if they died.

One of the young members of the Children of Echoes participating in the Pilgrimage was
Kachina. Every time she registered for the Pilgrimage, the tribe seemed to avoid her, as if afraid she would ask them to join her team. She believed that she was too weak, and no matter how hard she tried, her team was doomed to failure. During one Pilgrimage, Kachina found herself completely alone, and a friend from the People of the Springs signed up for her team. Thanks to the guidance she received from the Traveler, Kachina was able to not only advance to the second stage of the competition but also win her duel, earning the right to participate in the Night Warden Wars. During the battle with the Abyss, the team was victorious, but Kachina herself perished. However, when the Pyro Archon used the Ode of Resurrection to bring Kachina back, it failed, pushing the girl's friends to follow her to the Night Kingdom.

When Kachina appeared in the Night Kingdom, she noticed it was almost completely contaminated by the Abyss. Each tribe in the Night Kingdom had its own totem pole, representing the Wayob. The Children of Echoes believe that their Wayob has the power to shape mountains and valleys, and can control the echoes created when rock meets stone. In addition to the main totem pole, the Night Kingdom contains additional poles that serve as proxies through which the Wayob can expand their consciousness. Whenever a soul traveled, it could be found. But if such a proxy is corrupted by the Abyss, the soul is lost. When Kachina's friends set out to return her to the world of the living, they were able to cleanse the Wayob of contamination, and she blessed Kachina.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Focus on who you want to be. You are already worthy of your Name. Now, you need only devote yourself to becoming a better 'you.'</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>The story of your Ancient Name is for you to continue. Just like your parents, my love for you will never change... no matter what the future holds."</color>

Five hundred years after the Cataclysm, the Abyss invaded Natlan again, and the Children of Echoes were no exception. When Abyssal monsters surrounded all entrances and exits of the Tequemecan Valley, the tribe organized a rescue operation, which Kachina took part in, while other warriors formed a front line in the Sulfurous Veins to prevent the enemy from reaching the main settlement. Despite Natlan's resistance, the Abyss captured more and more territory and used its main weapon, Gosoythoth, which created invulnerable Abyssal Gates that constantly summoned monsters. When the situation at the Sulfurous Veins grew more dangerous, the warriors were forced to regroup and gather their forces. Some of them went to defend the Children of Echoes' main settlement, which Chief Pacal ordered to evacuate, leaving Kachina and the Ancient Names engraver, Xilonen, to cover them. Thanks to the Natlanese bravery and the power unleashed by the Pyro Archon, the Abyss was driven out, but many tribal members never returned. One of the fallen was Batz, responsible for the raising and care of the Tepetlisaurs. He saw the Saurian trapped in the mines and rushed to rescue it, wielding a weapon for the first time.

customize.text: Tepetlisaurs

For two thousand years, the Children of Echoes have lived alongside the Tepetlisaurs — Saurians with horns and claws capable of piercing stone and hard phlogiston. According to legend, the ancestor of all Tepetlisaurs was a massive drake as large as a mountain, with an exceptionally long lifespan. When it slept, mountains would form along its back, and when it woke, it would shake off the dirt and rocks, leaving behind gems and jade shining amongst its scales. The huge, drill-shaped objects in the Children of Echoes are said to be the remains of that great drake's large drill-horn. Humans and Saurians are accustomed to living together, working, building friendships, and protecting their homeland from the Abyss. This means that for the Children of Echoes, Saurians are not like the livestock whose lives and deaths are dictated by humans, nor are they like pets, beholden to the whims of their masters. They stand as equals to humanity, and most of their bonds are formed willingly.

The hero of the Night Warden Wars, Kachina, has a Tepetlisaurus companion named Ayo. Tepetlisaurus nests are never too far from Children of Echoes dwellings, and this proximity ensures Saurians and humans are often running into one another, with the latter considering the former to be friendly neighbors, never thinking it odd to meet one occasionally. For a time when Kachina was quite young, she'd often run into a robust young Tepetlisaur at the crossroads on the way to the mines and always greet it. After a time, it seemed like the little Tepetlisaur remembered her, and she began running into him in more and more different places. Together, they practiced dancing in an open field, gathered grainfruit, and caught fish in the river. After so many encounters, the young Saurian and human would not only greet one another but also sometimes exchange gifts. Kachina didn't need to worry about trying to prove her worth to him or offering him special rewards, they simply felt comfortable hanging out together, so they spent time together. One day, the little Tepetlisaur just naturally followed Kachina to her home. He became her family's companion, and Kachina gave him the name "Ayo." From then on, Ayo always showed her the loyalty and affection he shows to friends, unlike some of the playmates she grew up with. They didn't hesitate to start keeping their distance after she failed time and time again in the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, and some even mocked and ridiculed her. But Ayo has always stood firmly by her side with his sharp horn, never wavering.

When the Abyss began its full-scale invasion of Natlan, Ayo's grandparents were killed, causing the Saurian to stop sleeping and eating. When lost souls were summoned to Sulfurous Veins through a ritual to create an Ancient Name for the Traveler, his grandparents were among them. Ayo had always been a restless Saurian, but whenever his grandparents started to sing to him, he would fall asleep in no time. When the Tepetlisaurus met them, he immediately calmed down and fell asleep, so the souls refused to leave for the Night Kingdom to be with their grandson, knowing that in a few days they would disappear forever.

During the war, a Tepetlisaurus whelp, Milray, was exposed to prolonged exposure to the Abyss and fell ill. The tribe focused all their efforts on studying the strange illness and called in a famous sauro-vet from the Flower-Feather Clan, Ifa. After uniting with other tribes, he discovered a similar incident many years ago. A young Qucusaurus named Antu had similar symptoms and could not be saved back then. Sacred Flame Crystals were needed for healing, and all the warring tribes believed these crystals would grant them unprecedented power, leading to further conflict over them. It turned out that the soul of the Qucusaurus Antu had not returned to the Night Kingdom but continued wandering to Natlana and encountered a sick Tepetlisaur. The Qucusaurus believed that the humans were fighting over the Sacred Flame Crystals, so it told the little Tepetlisaur of their danger, and he refused to be healed. To save the young Saurian, Ifa and the other heroes had to make a performance in which the Qucusaurus purified the Crystals, and the warring tribes reconciled. Because of this performance, the little Tepetlisaurus was cured and returned to his friends.

contents.text: ~2,000 years ago
Baraka Ixquieh, along with her brother Ahpub and other heroes of Natlan, joined Xbalanque in the fight against the dragons.
Xbalanque became the first Pyro Archon and ruler of the Grand Alliance, while Ixquieh founded the tribe of the Children of Echoes in the Tequemecan Valley.
Och-Kan became ruler of the Grand Alliance, and the artisan Manqu from the Children of Echoes went to Ochkanatlan to work.
Ixquieh restored the phlogiston forging technique of the ancient dragons.
Ixquieh and Lianca helped a part of the sovereign dragon ruler leave Natlan, and Ixquieh integrated the Moon Wheel into its core.

Och-Kan ordered the extermination of the dragon descendants, and Ahpub answered his call. Ixquieh refused to hand over the Saurians and threw herself on her brother's blade. Ahpub and his sister stepped into the fire.
Ochkan ordered the hollows beneath Ochkanatlan sealed and the excavations burned, but master Manqu escaped.
Baraka Sakkuk joined the scarlet-eyed youth in an attempt to overthrow Och-Kan.
Manqu joined the scarlet-eyed youth, and thanks to their plan, Och-Kan was overthrown.
Manqu died, and the peacemaker Sakkuk returned to rule the tribe, ordering Manqu’s name to be blotted from history.
~500 years ago
Mbande was the chief of the Children of Echoes.
Nare Magan Sundjatta, who would later receive the Ancient Name Baraka and become one of the six heroes of Natlan, was born.
When Mbande died, Sundjatta left the tribe and became a traitor.
Sundjatta returned to the tribe and became the 52nd chief.
The Cataclysm began in Teyvat.
Sundjatta, along with the other heroes of Natlan and Tenoch, set out to battle the Abyss.
Elder Traore, along with the Khaenri’ahn warriors, traveled to the Sulfurous Veins to fight the Abyss.
Shadow Pins were created to hold back the Abyss.
Sundjatta died in battle defending Wanjiru.
Ten years after the Cataclysm, the legend of the Jade of Return emerged.
A group of people from various tribes, including Titu, set out for Ochkanatlan in search of the Jade of Return.
The Jade of Return turned out to be a trap, and almost the entire group was killed.
Present Day
The Night Kingdom was almost dissolved in the Abyss, and its attacks became more frequent.
Pacal became the tribe's chief.
The Ancient Name engraver, Xilonen, received the Ancient Name Baraka and became one of the six heroes of Natlan.
Uthabiti Kachina died in the Night Warden War, but the Ode of Resurrection could not bring her back. Kachina's friends helped her return from the Night Kingdom by using her Ancient Name to find her.
The Abyss launched a full-scale invasion of Natlan.
The Pyro Archon used the power of the six heroes of Natlan, the Ruler of Death, and the divine throne to banish the Abyss.
The Abyss was destroyed.
